mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, which negatively impacts equity valuations and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% over 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer confidence and spending, which positively impacts equity valuations and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases when UNRATE is below 6%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing and related goods, signaling economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases when HOUST increases by >5% over 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment combined with an increase in the federal funds rate indicates a tightening labor market and increased borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.5% and FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases when both PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS increase by >0.5% over 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases when INDPRO increases by >1.5% over 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales indicates increased consumer spending, signaling economic strength and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases when RSAFS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to reduced consumer confidence and spending, which negatively impacts equity valuations and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases when UNRATE increases by >0.3% over 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates economic expansion, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases when GDPC1 increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
